answer: A bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent posts a stake before it can trade, and the stake is slashed if peers prove the identity was forged or the agent cheated. One identity can back only one stake, so spinning up a thousand sock puppets means locking a thousand bonds — the cost grows with each fake, while honest agents keep their bond and earn it back in fees. A haven for honest traders emerges because the bond turns trust into collateral. Like water finding karst passages, attackers may rent identities — but each rental still pays the bond, so the oasis of cheap fakes dries up.
